question:
**Case Study 7: System Consistency in Market Equilibrium**

A market reports the prices of three interdependent goods $p_1$, $p_2$, $p_3$ are related by $\begin{aligned} p_1 + 2p_2 + p_3 &= 7 \\ 2p_1 - p_2 + 3p_3 &= 8 \\ p_1 - 3p_2 + 2p_3 &= 6 \end{aligned}$ Due to a new policy, suppliers ask whether a unique pricing solution exists, and if so, what it is.

a) Write the system in matrix form and check for consistency using determinants.

b) Using the matrix method, solve for the unique price if it exists.

c) Comment: What would a zero determinant indicate about the market? How would you detect infinitely many/no solutions in this context using minors and adjugate?
explanation:
a)
$A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 3 \\ 1 & -3 & 2\end{bmatrix}$, $X=\begin{bmatrix}p_1 \\ p_2 \\ p_3\end{bmatrix}$, $B=\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ 8 \\ 6\end{bmatrix}$

Calculate $|A|$.

Expand along row 1.
$|A| = 1\begin{vmatrix}-1 & 3 \\ -3 & 2\end{vmatrix} -2\begin{vmatrix}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{vmatrix}+1\begin{vmatrix}2 & -1 \\ 1 & -3\end{vmatrix}$

First: $-1\times2-3\times-3 = -2+9=7$
Second: $2\times2-3\times1=4-3=1$
Third: $2\times-3-(-1)\times1 = -6+1=-5$

So,
$|A|=1\times7 -2\times1 + 1\times(-5) = 7-2-5=0$
System is singular.

b)
Since $|A|=0$, check $(adj~A)B$. If $(adj~A)B\ne0$, inconsistent (no solution). Otherwise, perhaps infinitely many solutions.

Calculate adjugate, then multiply by $B$.
(For brevity, outline: compute cofactors, then adjugate, then $(adj~A)B$ to check consistency.)

c)
Zero determinant: market is overdetermined or relationships are dependent—no unique price solution.
If $(adj~A)B = 0$, infinitely many prices can meet supplies. If not, system is inconsistent, meaning at least one constraint can't be met: a market disequilibrium.

options.A:
a) $|A|\ne0$, so the system has a unique solution.
b) The unique price vector is $X=\begin{bmatrix}1\\2\\3\end{bmatrix}$.
c) A zero determinant would still imply a unique market solution.
options.B:
a) $|A|=0$, so the system has infinitely many solutions.
b) Since $R_3=R_2-R_1$ and $6=8-7$, infinitely many price vectors exist.
c) A zero determinant always means infinitely many solutions.
options.C:
a) $AX=B$, where $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2&1\\2&-1&3\\1&-3&2\end{bmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{bmatrix}7\\8\\6\end{bmatrix}$; $|A|=0$, so no unique solution exists.
b) Since $R_3=R_2-R_1$ but $6\ne8-7$, the system is inconsistent and has no solution.
c) A zero determinant means no unique solution; consistency is checked using row relations or $\operatorname{adj}(A)B$.
options.D:
a) $|A|=1$, so the system is non-singular.
b) The unique solution is $p_1=7$, $p_2=8$, $p_3=6$.
c) A zero determinant means the market equations are independent.
